days.title: Northern Nature and Royal Sights
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Raukar von Byrum
stops.detail: In the north, the Raukar of Byrum indicate that the island rose from the sea.

stops.name: Blå Jungfrun
stops.detail: Between the mainland and the island, in the middle of the Kalmar Strait, lies the granite island of Blå Jungfrun (German: Blue Virgin), protected as a national park.

stops.name: Sandviks Kvarn
stops.detail: Other well-known mills are the mills of Lerkaka, of Störlinge, Sandviks Kvarn, the mill of Strandtorp and the Jordhamn scrubbing mill.

stops.name: Schloss Solliden
stops.detail: Near the largest city on Öland, Borgholm, the Swedish royal family has its summer residence, Solliden Palace.

days.driving: Allow time between these sights; local travel times are not verified and conditions vary.

days.title: Southern Landscapes and Ancient Monuments
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Stora Alvaret
stops.detail: As the soil layer is thin due to erosion, large parts of the island – especially in the south – consist of a karst and heath landscape (Stora Alvaret) with corresponding fauna.

stops.name: Blå rör
stops.detail: During this period, large burial mounds were created, including the Blå rör, the largest of the approximately 100 tumuli on the island.

stops.name: Gettlinge
stops.detail: Ship settings (Gettlinge) and treuddar (Vi alvar, Resmo, Segerstad) are, however, rare.

stops.name: Eketorp
stops.detail: The large castle complexes such as Gråborg, Ismantorp and Eketorp date from the period between 400 and 550 AD.
